id: Summer in the City: Exploring Entertainment on the Thomas Ward Map-Katherine Mansfield House & Garden, 25 Tinakori Rd, Thorndon, Wellington-Event Finder
name: Summer in the City: Exploring Entertainment on the Thomas Ward Map
venue: Katherine Mansfield House & Garden, 25 Tinakori Rd, Thorndon, Wellington
long_description:
Space is limited so booking is essential!

Where did Wellingtonians head when it was time to have fun in the 1890s? Join historian Elizabeth Cox as she explores the entertainment options for young and old that can be found on the Thomas Ward map.

The Thomas Ward map was drawn by surveyor Thomas Ward for Wellington City Council. First completed in 1891, it was then updated for the next decade. It recorded the footprint of every building in the city, from Thorndon in the north and across the teeming, inner-city slums of Te Aro to Berhampore in the south. The map detailed every house, outdoor toilet and garden shed in the city, as well as hotels, theatres, oyster saloons, brothels, shops, stables, Parliament, kāinga, Town Belt, ‘lunatic asylum’, hospital and much more, down to the detail of the street lights.
The stories of the places recorded on this map and the people who lived in them are the subject of Elizabeth’s award-winning book 'Mr Ward’s Map: Victorian Wellington Street by Street'.

You can also visit the exhibition 'Growing Up on Mr Ward’s Map: Stories of Young Lives in Victorian Wellington'. Created especially for Katherine Mansfield House & Garden by Elizabeth and the book’s designer Jo Bailey, the exhibition uses the Thomas Ward map to examine what it was like to grow up in the city in the 1890s, featuring voices, stories and photographs of the city's children and teenagers.

Please note that this event will take place upstairs, see the Accessibility page of the Katherine Mansfield House & Garden website for more information.

name: Young Photographer Award 2026
venue: Little Theatre, 2 Queens Dr, Lower Hutt
long_description:
Join us for a special evening celebrating the creativity, achievements and unique perspectives of young photographers from across the Wellington region and beyond.

Following the success of our inaugural awards in 2025, which brought together nearly 200 children, families, photographers and supporters, the Young Photographer Awards are returning for another inspiring celebration!

Organised by The Art of Seeing Academy, the awards recognise young people aged 7–18 who have participated in our photography workshops throughout the year.

For many of these young photographers, this may be the first time their work has been publicly celebrated. Every photograph tells a story, and every young photographer brings a different way of seeing the world.

What to expect on the night

This year's ceremony will bring together young photographers, their families, professional photographers and our wider creative community.

The evening will feature:

Young Photographer Awards presentation: Celebrating selected young photographers and recognising their creativity, effort and achievements.
Five inspiring guest speakers: Professional photographers sharing their experiences, creative journeys and stories from behind the lens.
Young photographers' work: A celebration of the images, ideas and perspectives developed through our workshops.
A community celebration: An opportunity to come together, support young talent and recognise the importance of creativity in young people's lives.

Meet our guest speakers

Fairlie Atkinson

Fairlie is a photography teacher at Kāpiti College who has helped students achieve national recognition through awards and exhibitions. Passionate about creativity and community, she encourages young photographers to use their images to tell meaningful stories, advocate for causes they care about and make a positive difference.

Tara Swan

Tara is a wildlife photographer and ecologist with over a decade of experience working with rare birds. Her photography focuses on Aotearoa's native wildlife and Kaimanawa horses. She'll share how photography can tell the stories of our natural world and inspire greater care for wildlife and conservation.

Dave Allen

With over 30 years of experience in photography and videography, Dave will explore how to build confidence as a photographer. He'll share insights into managing self-doubt, stepping outside your comfort zone and recognising the creative strengths that come with being yourself.

Stephen Garner

Stephen has been taking photographs since receiving his first camera at age six. He loves street, travel and documentary photography, often accompanied by his two wind-up corgis, Dante and Virgil. He'll share his playful approach to finding inspiration and overcoming creative blocks.

Emmeline Plachecki

Emmeline is a New Zealand photographer specialising in equine photography. Combining her understanding of horses with a creative eye, she captures the emotions, personalities and connections that make each horse unique. She'll explore how photography can tell stories that go beyond what we see

Throughout 2026, The Art of Seeing Academy has continued to introduce children and teenagers to photography through hands-on workshops across the Lower North Island region. Some participants pick up a camera for the first time. Others return to develop their skills, explore new ideas and discover their own photographic style. Our workshops encourage young people to slow down, observe their surroundings, express themselves and build confidence through creativity. We welcome young people of all abilities, backgrounds and learning needs.

The Young Photographer Awards are an opportunity to recognise their progress and celebrate what they have achieved.

Come and celebrate with us!

venue: MEOW, 9 Edward St, Wellington
long_description:
One of dubstep’s most distinctive and influential producers, Silkie brings more than two decades of UK underground history to the dancefloor.

Born and raised in Hammersmith, West London, Solomon Rose emerged through the early UK garage and grime scenes before becoming a key figure in dubstep’s formative years. After discovering the sound through pirate radio and London’s legendary FWD>> parties, he co-founded Antisocial Entertainment in 2004 and became a regular presence on Rinse FM, helping shape a new generation of bass music.

Signing to Mala’s Deep Medi Musik in 2008, Silkie developed a sound entirely his own. Deep sub-bass meets warm synths, jazz harmony, funk, soul and R&B, creating a melodic, musical take on 140 that helped define what became known as dubstep’s “purple” sound. His acclaimed catalogue includes City Limits Vol. 1, City Limits Vol. 2, Fractals and Panorama, alongside a long run of club-focused singles and EPs.

More recently, Silkie has continued pushing both sides of his musical identity. He relaunched Antisocial Records, returned to his UK garage roots through Bedroom Rat Records under his real name Solomon Rose, and continues to champion bass-heavy, soulful electronic music through radio, releases and production.

Expect deep dubstep, heavyweight bass pressure, soulful UK garage and unmistakable West London flavour from one of the genre’s true originals.

SUPPORT: BABETECH (Te Aupōuri, Te Whānau-ā-Āpanui)
Te Whanganui-a-Tara-based Māori selectress BABETECH brings her whakapapa and connection to whenua into the club, blending deep basslines, percussion and soundsystem culture. Moving between dubstep, dub, reggae, footwork and grime, she’s shared stages with Loefah, Plastician, Half Queen and Lady Shaka. Rooted in culture, driven by bass and made for the dancefloor.

long_description:
From Friday the 27th to Monday the 30th of November, the tracks of Zealandia will be teeming with citizen scientists (that’s you!) taking part in the Great Southern BioBlitz.

A bioblitz is a great way for communities to get involved in the natural world, learning more about the fauna, flora, and fungi living right under our noses. Spend the weekend taking photos of as many different species as you can to upload to iNaturalist, and watch as experts come along behind you and identify what you have found!

And how can we make that even more exciting? By making a friendly competition out of the event with neighbouring cities by having the most observations recorded! Look out Christchurch!

Anyone can participate and contribute to the wider data base of species in Aotearoa New Zealand. We can’t wait to see your observations from all across the Wellington region, whether that’s here at Zealandia or in your own backyard.

Learn more about the Great Southern BioBlitz.

Coin Laundry has been Tom Garden's project for 15 years of writing and recording. The first lineup played its debut gig in Dunedin in early 2020 — a week before COVID hit. After relocating to Wellington a year ago, Tom rebuilt the band with Marie Dutilloy on bass and Cy Manlunas on drums, and Coin Laundry is back gigging and writing new music, building momentum in the Wellington scene.

Having sold out their DIY first gig at the start of October, Dogmatic are raring to play again. Drawing from elements of grunge and indie, they'll play a set of dynamic rock music that's sure to get you moving.

Dressed in Wax: A four piece indie rock band drawing inspiration from 90s bands such as The Pixies, Archers of Loaf, Pavement, Modest Mouse, Sunny Day Real Estate. At times emotional and relentlessly melodic.

Come on down to Valhalla for some midweek fun. $10 on the door. Bring a friend.
